subtopics.title: Relative Prices — the Signal Buyers Actually Read

questions.question: Rice costs R30 a kilogram and maize meal costs R15. The relative price of rice is:
options: Two kilograms of maize meal per kilogram of rice
Half a kilogram of maize meal per kilogram of rice

questions.question: If every price in the economy doubled overnight and all incomes doubled too, a rational shopper's choices would:
options: Stay the same — no relative price changed

questions.question: Only rice doubles in price while maize meal holds steady. Maize meal has become:
options: Relatively cheaper, even though its own tag never moved

questions.question: A change in the price of the good ITSELF causes:
options: A shift of the entire demand curve
A movement along its demand curve
A shift of the supply curve for its substitute

subtopics.title: Substitutes and Complements — and Their Graphs in Words

questions.question: Butter jumps from R60 to R85 a brick after a dairy shortage. In the margarine market this causes:
options: A movement along the margarine demand curve
A leftward shift of margarine demand
A rightward shift of the entire margarine demand curve
No change, since margarine's price is unchanged

questions.question: Which pair are complements?
options: A smart TV and a streaming subscription

questions.question: The price of mobile data rises. The demand curve for streaming subscriptions:
options: Shifts to the left — data and streaming are partners

questions.question: The symmetry rule says:
options: Substitutes and complements always shift demand the same way
For substitutes, the related good's price and our good's demand move in the same direction; for complements, in opposite directions
For complements, the related good's price and our good's demand move in the same direction
Related goods never affect each other's demand

subtopics.title: Product Markets and Factor Markets — the Loop That Connects Shops to Jobs

questions.question: Factor markets are where:
options: Goods and services are sold to households
The factors of production are hired — labour, capital, property
Prices are set by the state

questions.question: The demand for electricians is called DERIVED demand because:
options: Electricians derive satisfaction from their work
It is borrowed from the demand for the products their work delivers, like powered homes
It is calculated from a formula

questions.question: A rooftop-solar boom raises installers' wages and panel prices. Run BACKWARD through the loop, these higher factor prices:
options: Shift product supply leftward, lifting installation prices
Shift product supply rightward, cutting prices

questions.question: The circular flow connects the two market types because:
options: Firms pay wages out of fixed costs
Product markets and factor markets never interact
Wages paid in factor markets become household income, which returns as spending in product markets

subtopics.title: The Four Market Structures — a First Map

questions.question: One cabbage farmer among hundreds, selling identical produce with free entry, operates under:
Coffee shops and hair salons — many sellers, easy entry, differentiated offerings — illustrate:
The defining feature of oligopoly is:
options: Interdependence — each firm anticipates its rivals' reactions before moving price

questions.question: Perfect competition is the only 'perfect' market because:
options: In the other three structures sellers hold some power over price
Its sellers earn the highest profits
Its products are the best quality

subtopics.title: The Shelf Decides — Rice, Maize Meal and the Compared Price

questions.question: The only price your feet actually obey in the aisle is:
options: The money price on the tag alone
The compared price — one good measured against the other

questions.question: A poor harvest pushes maize meal to R25. In the rice aisle, rice's demand curve:
options: Slides along itself as rice gets cheaper
Steps to the right — at every rice price there are now more willing buyers

questions.question: Bread turns pricey, and polony sales sag even though polony's tag never changed. This is because bread and polony are:

subtopics.title: Every Job Is Hiding Inside Something Somebody Buys

questions.question: An electrician has a job ultimately because:
options: Somebody wants the lights to stay on — labour demand is derived from product demand

questions.question: A solar spree hits the Western Cape. Which factor-market effect follows automatically?
options: Wages for accredited installers get bid up

questions.question: The electrician's fatter pay packet 'goes home and becomes spending at the shops'. This illustrates:
options: The circular flow linking factor income to product-market spending
A movement along the labour supply curve

subtopics.title: Count the Sellers — From the Market Stalls to the Water Pipes

questions.question: At the farmers' market with forty identical spinach stalls, charging R5 more than your neighbour means:
options: Your customers drift three steps sideways — you are a price taker

questions.question: A hair salon can charge a little more than its neighbours because:
options: Its service is differentiated — famous fades, walk-ins, comfortable chairs

questions.question: Domestic airlines watching each other before touching a fare, with billions needed to launch a rival, illustrate:
options: Oligopoly — few sellers, hard entry, interdependence

questions.question: The ladder of price power says that as sellers grow fewer and entry grows harder:
options: Price power grows — from taking the price, to nudging it, to watching rivals, to making it
